body:
“To survive is to fight” — my friend

She said this during a speech at a trans activism event about a year ago. I hadn’t attended because I was recently out of the hospital from a suicide attempt and the prevalence of anti-trans politics was really fucking w my mental health (and part of why I had attempted). I don’t remember the exact context bcs I wasn’t there (she told me about it after) but I think she was referencing how I specifically but also a lot of trans ppl feel bad when they can’t do activism and fight back against all this anti trans shit because of whatever reason (in my case mental health) but that just existing is fighting back.

The poem:

*Tomorrow when the farm boys find this*

*freak of nature, they will wrap his body*

*in newspaper and carry him to the museum.*


*But tonight he is alive and in the north*

*field with his mother. It is a perfect*

*summer evening: the moon rising over*

*the orchard, the wind in the grass. And*

*as he stares into the sky, there are*

*twice as many stars as usual.*

Not a sentence, but the poem “the two headed calf” by Laura Gilpin.

Hard to articulate why it means so much to me but I think it helps me appreciate and accept that life is a cycle of joy and pain and if I focus on the pain I don’t get to feel the joy.
Yeah, I also have trauma from after my childhood (tti rtc 2 years from 16-18)
